title: Lists and syntax inside Peano arithmetic

based_on.title: Provability logic: models within models in Peano Arithmetic
An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems, second edition, corrected Logic Matters reprint

summary: Concrete list traversals and syntax routines retain their equations at nonstandard codes.
abstract: Proof transformations need to recognize formulas, substitute terms, and keep track of variable names. Before Peano arithmetic can verify such transformations, it must prove the basic laws of the numerical routines that perform them. We construct list operations and syntax operations from specific recursive programs, then prove their recognition, substitution, and freshness properties inside arithmetic. The proofs explain why decreasing expression codes and tables of earlier answers support the required inductions. This gives the later proof checker reliable operations at every value allowed by arithmetic, including codes in nonstandard models that do not describe an ordinary finite expression.
